r.name: C01 - Villadossola-Alpe Baldana bivio C05
r.description: Route from Villadossola, through the fractions of Piaggio Sopra and Gaggitti, going up, passing through the pastures of Corticcio, Basciumo Sotto and Sopra, reaches the Baldana alp. From here, joning with the path C05, you reach the S. Giacomo alp.

r.name: A53 - Pallanzeno-Alpe Corticcio
r.description: Route from Pallanzeno to Alpe Corticcio passing from the Enel Basin from where you have a nice view of the lower Ossola Valley. From Alpe Corticcio join the path C01 for Basciumo and S. Giacomo

r.name: D12 - S. Bernardo - Monte del Dente
r.description: The route climbs from S. Bernardo the ridge first wooded, then meadow with views on both sides on two lakes, reaching Verrosso Peak

r.name: C14 - Rivera - Bordo - Cheggio - Alpe Cavallo
r.description: Route from Rivera, fraction of Viganella, leads to Alpe Cavallo passing by the villages of Bordo and Cheggio absolutely to visit

r.name: F03 - Alpe Salviggia - Lorino
r.description: Until Prato Grande, in the woods, well kept. From Pratogrande to Crucible 1524, very steep and quite clean. From the dirty but well marked dirt path, clear signs of fresh paint

r.name: F01 - Varzo - Passo Pian Pumper
r.description: Well marked and clean forest path, high marked and evident: lack of water

r.name: F38a sentiero Filosi Agro Fuori 1787 Monte Teggiolo 2394
r.description: Well-marked and evident trail of the ridge. last stretch to the summit, short rock passages protected by chains

r.description: Ascent to sight on broad meadow ridge, not marked but obvious

r.name: F97 - Bivio F10 - Passo delle Possette
r.description: Up to Valle Traccia EE, then dirt track and beautiful trail

r.name: F98 - Bugliaga - Passo delle Possette
r.description: in woodland up to Casalavera 1540, then open spaces up to the pass. Always clean path

r.name: F32 - Iselle - Alpe Pianezzoni
r.description: From Iselle a short stretch of state road, then a path through the woods. Well marked and visible path. at times steep

r.name: F38 - Trasquera - Agro Dentro
r.description: Steep path up to Agro Outside 1787 m, but always well marked, clear and clean

r.name: F40 - bivio F00 - Alpe Agro Dentro

r.name: F42 - Bugliaga - Bivio F32

r.name: C05c - Alpe Mandariola sotto - Alpe Corticcio
r.description: Path which, together with the C05b, connecting the lower pastures (800 m asl) of the municipalities of Villadossola and Borgomezzavalle

r.description: Path which, together with the C05b, connecting the lower pastures (800 m asl) of the municipalities of Villadossola and Borgomezzavalle

r.name: C05 - Seppiana - Alpe S. Giacomo
r.description: The route from Seppiana reaches, passing through the mountain pastures of Crotto, Mandariola and Baldana, the Alpe S. Giacomo and the oratory dedicated to the Saint. In honor of the saint every year at the end of July the Autani di Seppiana takes place

r.name: C07 - Seppiana - Alpe Zii - Alpe San Giacomo
r.description: Path that from Seppiana, passing from the Alpe Zii and from the Colma lake cross, reaches the Alpe S. Giacomo and the oratory dedicated to the Saint. In his honor every year at the end of July the Autani di Seppiana takes place

C27 - Antronapiana - Bivio C99 (Coronette)
r.description: Long path and, in the last part, challenging. From Antronapiana you go up all the Valle Loranco up to Lake Ciapivul to end up at the junction with C99 at the Coronette

r.name: F50b - Ciamporino - Alpe Solcio
r.description: Superb panoramic half mountainside route, along the path of Alta Via Val Divedro, along pastures still loaded for grazing of cattle with refurbished huts for holiday use where the original features have been maintained.

r.name: A47 - Fomarco - Pizzo Camino
r.description: A long and strenuous route with challenging sections, especially from Alpe il Ghiaccio onward. But the spectacular views you can enjoy during the climb and from the summit are worth the effort.

r.name: F12 da Maulone sp per S. Domenico 957 mt a bivio F10 1400 mt

r.description: after 120 m of ascent on the rail, continue on dirt until the end

r.name: F14 - San Domenico - Alpe Coatè
r.description: The route takes place on a path alternating with asphalt and tractors

r.name: A03 - Villadossola - Colletto Moncucco
r.description: The path A03 starts from Villadossola and develops on the eastern side of Moncucco up to the hill below the summit, at the junction with path D01 that goes up from Domodossola

r.name: A01 - La Via Alta (Crosiggia - Boschetto)
r.description: The Via Alta - It was the road that connected the valleys, Bognanco and Antrona, without going down to the valley bottom

r.name: D00 - Quarta sezione: Graniga - Monte Calvario
r.description: Fourth section of the Via del Monscera also known as Via Stockalper through villages, gorges, the thermal baths of Bognanco, the Torchio di Monteossolano and the Sacro Monte Calvario

r.name: B01 - Castiglione - Alpe Marmazzuolo fuori
r.description: A route that is sometimes challenging and that goes from Calasca Catiglione to Marmazzuolo di Fuori passing through Pograsso

r.name: A51 - Cimamulera - Pizzo Castello
r.description: Service trail to the pastures of the South/East side of Pizzo Castello with panoramic views over the valleys, the junction with C07 connects the Colma and S. Giacomo mountain pastures

r.name: C02 - Sogno - Moncucco
r.description: The path presents a first part in the wood, then, starting from the alp La Colma, with a higher degree of difficulty, it develops on the ridge till to the peak of Moncucco

r.name: C12 - Viganella - Alpe Barco - Alpe Cavallo
r.description: This is, of the three possible, the longest and most demanding route to reach the Alpe Cavallo

r.name: C96 - Prato - Alpe Colma dei Prei
r.description: This route, from Prato to Colma dei Prei, is part of the GTA stage that from Antrona, loc.ty Cheggio arrives precisely at the refuge of Colma.

r.name: C09 - Viganella - Alpe Colma dei Prei
r.description: Path that from Viganella reaches the pastures of Colma passing from Alpe la Piana

r.name: C16 - San Pietro, bivio C00 - Alpe Cavallo
F16 - San Domenico - Monte Cistella
r.description: Long but rewarding climb. From the summit of Monte Cistella the view is spectacular at 360 °. Suitable for normal hikers except for a short final stretch under the summit which requires a short climb, there is a chain (2022).

r.name: C32 - Forcola di Cheggio
r.description: Panoramic route that connects the Troncone Valley with the Loranco Valley through the Forcola pass and its mountain pastures

r.name: C23 - Campliccioli, bivio C00 - Alpe Lombraoro sotto, bivio C00
r.description: Path that, starting from the Campliccioli dam, crosses the most interesting mountain pastures on the right bank of the Troncone torrent

r.name: D05 - Località Torno (quota 443) - Alpe Foppiano (quota 1160)
r.description: path up to Alpe Bei 775 m, then dirt road, to Cascina Vè 996, then with a long traverse in the woods, up to the Domobianca ski slopes

r.name: C23a - Alpe Lombraoro inf., bivio C00 - Alpe Lareccio, bivio C23
r.description: Path connecting the C00 and C23, the two main paths of the Troncone Valley, shortening the tour in proximity the Lareccio alp

r.name: B04a - Pecciola - Drocala
r.description: Near the hamlet of Pecciola, at the crossroads along the Strà Granda (B00), the path that passes through Ielmala and Ca Bison reaches Drocala.

r.name: B04 - Castiglione - Erbalunga
r.description: At the beginning of Castiglione, at the crossroads along the Strà Granda (B00), the path begins that goes from Drocala to Alpe Prer and then to Alpe Aloro and ends on the Colma ridge in Erbalunga.

r.name: C04a - Varchignoli - Vallemiola
r.description: From the megalithic site of Varchignoli, a hamlet of Villadossola, passing through the terraces of Valin Bianch and Zasca reaches Vallemiola, an ancient hamlet of Montescheno.

r.name: C10 - Seppiana - Alpe Ortighè
r.description: In front of the church of Seppiana the mule track for Zonca begins. From Zonca begins the path which, crossing Alpe Taia above, Alpe Scariola and Alpe Casale, ends at Alpe Ortighè at the crossroads with path C08.

r.name: C34 - Lago di Campliccioli - Lago di Camposecco
r.description: Upstream of the Campliccioli dam, after the bridge over the Rio Banella, (junction C00) begins the path that crosses the mountain pastures, Curzut, Banella, Scarone and Loraccio and reaches the Camposecco dam (junction C99).

r.name: A51c - loc.tà Coloria, bivio A00a - Trogo - Colletto - Costa dell'Oraccio, bivio A51A
A53d - ul Dric, Paset Cesar, bivio A53 (fontana) - Alpe Basciumo sopra, bivio C01

r.description: Half-way path, little frequented, but pleasant. Steep salt to reach the flower path or F50 to Alpe Veglia

r.name: F95 - Varzo - Passo di Variola
r.description: F95 - Varzo - Passo di Variola - Salita molto impegnativa di oltre 1860 metri di dislivello che partendo da Varzo ci conduce al passo di Variola .Il percorso ripido a tratti esposto , esposto a nord, assenza di acqua
Old path and mule track connecting Trasquera and Varzo

r.name: F36b - Gebbo - San Domenico
r.description: Mule track from Trasquera to S. Domenico, which crosses the various hamlets

r.name: C97 - bivio C27/C97 - Passo di Andolla
r.description: We are on the Strada Antronesca, one of the routes leading from the Ossola Valleys to Switzerland; from Antronapiana, follow trail C27 to Cheggio and Lago dei Cavalli, then take trail C97, passing the Andolla Refuge and finally reaching the Andolla Pass

r.name: C06 - Montescheno - Alpi di Sogno - Cima Camughera
D13 - Bognanco - Pioi
r.description: A route that is exposed in parts and leads from Bognanco to Pioi. The route is of particular interest for those who want to travel along the lower valley following the two banks as part of a circular valley itinerary.

r.name: D04 - Gabbio - Cima Lariè
r.description: Historic paved mule track up to Monteossolano where the grape marc press is very interesting, then you climb up through traditional locality and high altitude pastures among larches and then the final ridge with vast panoramas

r.name: D06 - Costa d'Agrello
r.description: Long route in an isolated environment, through woods and ridges that are not very exposed and not very frequented

r.name: D18c - Pizzanco - bivio D98
r.description: Connecting route between Pizzanco and the Oriaccia and Vallaro mountain pastures continuing on the D98 route

r.name: D01 - Cappella di Marisch - Moncucco
r.description: From the Marish Chapel through the woods you reach Vallesone, cross the asphalt road and take the wide path that leads to Alpe Lusentino, then along the tracks and paths near the sky slopes you reach Alpe Torcelli and shortly after the final crest.

r.name: A51a - Moiachina - Alpe Propiano superiore
r.description: Alternative route to the mountain pastures of Propiano from Piedimulera but also from Pallanzeno with the variant A51d

D98 - Pragio bivio D00 - Passo della Preja
GTA: Molini di Calasca - Alpe del Lago
D99 - Bivio D08 - Passo di Variola
r.description: A low route for the Variola pass, the route, almost entirely on the hillside, follows the course of the Variola stream through the Dorca and Variola mountain pastures to lead to the pass of the same name

r.name: D10 - Alpe Paione - Passo di Paione
r.description: Starting from Alpe Paione the route allows you to visit the three Paioni lakes and takes us to the pass of the same name from which there is no route towards Switzerland.

r.name: D08a - Gomba -Vercengio
r.description: Mostly flat path that leads from the beautiful Gomba locality to Vercengio

r.name: D14a - Alpe Oriaccia - Lago di Oriaccia
r.description: Semi-abandoned and little-used path between Oriaccia and Lake Oriaccia.

r.name: D17 - bivio D19 - Passo d'Arnigo
r.description: Route to discover the wildest area of the Bognanco valley, we first encounter the Garione alp still used by shepherds in the summer months and then reach the Passo d'Arnigo from which you can access the Antrona valley with difficult paths

r.name: F01a - Alpe Lorino - Alpe Albiona
r.description: Path free of the hillside, little frequented, the only challenging stretch is the crossing of the Rio di Mezzodì, landslide, to be done very carefully

r.name: B20 - Vanzone - Bivio C21 presso Pizzo San Martino
D14 - Gomba - Passo di Oriaccia
r.description: Initially steep route follows the final stretch of the Vertical "La Veia" from Alpe Dente becomes a pleasant panoramic path halfway up the hill towards Lake Oriaccia a short stretch on a rocky slope leads to the pass.

r.name: D15 - Picciola bivio D19 - Bivio C06
r.description: A short stretch among beech woods leads us to Curtit where there is an ancient mine. Among meadows and high altitude pastures we reach the Scatta locality from here, halfway up the hill, we reach the Saudera locality and shortly after the C06 path

r.name: D19 - bivio D20 presso Picciola - Passo del Fornalino
r.description: Route for the Fornalino pass and the Antrona Valley, steep at times and exposed, poor signposts

r.name: C30 - Alpe Andolla sup., bivio C97/C30 - Alpe Corone inferiore
D08 - Bognanco Terme - Passo del Monscera
r.description: Easy but challenging route due to its length and altitude difference which passes through hamlets far from the road up to Alpe San Bernardo, from here following a forest road you reach Alpe Monscera and with a short path the Monscera Pass

r.name: D18 - Bivio D98 presso Alpe Vallaro - Passo di Pontimia
r.description: Route in the uncontaminated territories of the upper valley, you travel three passes and meet the Campo lakes to find yourself on the border in front of the Waissmiess

r.description: From Antronapiana, follow the mule track as far as Ponte delle Vacche; beyond this point, the path is rarely used, with fallen trees and vegetation. Passing through a forest of ancient chestnut trees, you reach the Alpe Corticcio.

r.description: A route connecting Cheggio with the neighboring Bognanco Valley via the Fornalino Pass. Every two years, it serves as the venue for a traditional gathering of the people from the Antrona and Bognanco valleys.

A47a - Gulo - Ca Zaine
r.description: The path halfway up the hillside leads us from Gulo to the pastures of Cà Zeine and Pograsso through the lesser-known side of the Anzasca valley. The wilder side certainly allows you to admire the many villages and hamlets on the opposite side

r.name: A01a - Gaggio - Sogno
r.description: Easy and panoramic path that crosses some hamlets of Villadossola on the eastern side of Moncucco until reaching Sogno

r.name: B12 - Madonna del Sassello - Alpe Vallar
B10 - Barzone di Calasca - Passo del Mottone
B08b - Calasca dentro - Bivio B08
r.description: There are no signs along the trail, except at Alpe Cascinolo, and no painted trail markers. From the start, you can tell the trail is no longer used; tall grass and shrubs make it difficult to see the faint trail.
